# headless turn (`grok --trust --session-id <uuid> -p "Reply with the word
# ready."`) plus one keeper-lane pty turn, each blocked once by a project
# Stop hook. The block reply ({"decision":"block","reason":...} on hook
# stdout) kept the agent working: Stop re-fired with stopHookActive=true and
# the final headless stdout carried the requested GROK_CONT_<session-id>
# token. grok wrote one scratch-scoped entry into
# ~/.grok/trusted_folders.toml when --trust was honored; the folder is a
# throwaway and no other grok config was read or written.
#
# The capability row stays "extension". The Stop CONTRACT above is real, but
# it was measured through a PROJECT hook in the scratch repo. Footnote's own
# route into grok is the Claude-plugin scan, and the live debug receipt
# (`grok --debug-file`) shows grok 1.0.34 discovering the fno plugin with
# has_hooks=true yet dispatching NONE of its hooks: on session_start,
# user_prompt_submit and stop only global (Claude settings compat) and
# project hooks ran. With no plugin hook dispatched, footnote's Stop gate
# never reaches grok, so a looping dispatch stays refused until grok
# dispatches plugin hooks or the plugin is installed through grok's own
# installer (an operator config change, out of scope for a measurement run).
